## 16. Noon Curveball — the assumption that broke and the revised design

*Written in a fresh agent session, reconstructed from Checkpoint `0b7f487b6e75`, **before any code
was edited**. Everything in §16 was captured in context, not explained verbally.*

### 16.1 The assumption the Curveball invalidated

Stated as narrowly as it can be:

> **entire-guard assumed that the record of what an agent changed is a single source with no
> format at all** — `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` against a local working tree.

Two things were baked into that and both are now false:

| Assumption | Why it is false after the Curveball |
|---|---|
| **Singular** — there is one record of the change | The agent's own transcript is now also a record, and it is a *different* record |
| **Format-free** — the record needs no parsing, so no format can change underneath us | The transcript arrives in at least two formats, one of which did not exist when the contract was designed |

And a third consequence the first two hide: **a transcript can describe work that `git` on this
machine cannot see at all** — a session run elsewhere, against another checkout, or interrupted
before anything was written. A verification path that only knows how to read a local diff cannot
even represent that situation, let alone judge it safely.

Track 3's card is therefore not a request for a new parser. It is a request to stop treating
"what changed" as a fact and start treating it as **evidence with a provenance and a confidence**
— which is the discipline §6 already applied to graph relations and checkpoint traps, and had
never applied to the diff.

### 16.2 Graph impact, run before editing

Per the card, impact analysis ran first. Raw JSON is committed under `evidence/curveball/`.

```bash
entire graph search --repo . --profile full \
  --query "determine which files the agent actually changed and adjudicate them against the contract"
entire graph impact --symbol changedSince --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol parseJson    --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol knownTraps   --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol verify       --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol adjudicate   --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
```

| Symbol | Callers found | What it changed about the plan |
|---|---|---|
| `changedSince` | 1 direct (`core.ts:100 verify`), 2 transitive (`cli.ts:31 main`, `server.ts`) | **The git adapter needs no change at all.** The new source is added *beside* it in `verify`, not inside it. This narrowed the edit. |
| `parseJson` | 2 direct (`knownTraps`, `impact`) | Give it a **sibling** `parseJsonl()` rather than modify it — neither existing caller is disturbed. |
| `knownTraps` | 1 direct (`core.ts:26 propose`) | The trap path has exactly one entry point, so a second trap *source* is a local change. |
| `verify` | 2 direct (`cli.ts:31 main`, `server.ts`) | Both transports must gain the new optional input, or the feature is unreachable from one of them. |
| `adjudicate` | 5 direct — **3 of them test files** (`adjudicate.test.ts`, `build.test.ts`, `e2e.test.ts`) | The decisive finding: every new field must be **additive and optional**, so all 33 existing tests keep compiling and passing *unmodified*. |

The blast radius is entirely inside `mcp/entire-guard/src`. **No Go module is touched**, which is
worth stating because §4A's cross-module drift risk is the one thing that would have made this a
wide change.

### 16.3 The two formats, pinned against real code

Neither format was guessed. The original was read out of this repository's own protocol types
(`agents/*/internal/protocol/types.go`, plus the integer values emitted in
`agents/*/internal/*/hooks.go`); the new one was read out of the attached fixture.

| | **Original** — Entire external-agent protocol | **New** — AcmeCode 1.4.2 (`track-3-agent-session.jsonl`) |
|---|---|---|
| Discriminator | `type` — an **integer** | `event` — a **string** |
| Lifecycle | `1` agent-spawn, `2` user-prompt-submit, `3` stop. `5` is emitted by goose and its meaning is **not documented in this repo** | `session_started` / `session_ended` (+ `status`, `duration_seconds`) |
| Changed files | `AgentSessionJSON.modified_files[] / new_files[] / deleted_files[]` — a **batch summary**; plus `tool_input.file_path` on tool events | `file_changed` events, **streamed one per edit**, with `change: modified\|created\|deleted`, `summary`, `lines_added`, `lines_removed` |
| Checkpoint | minted by Entire from the session | `checkpoint_created` carrying `checkpoint_id`, `git_commit`, `intent`, `summary`, **`open_questions[]`** |
| Other events | `HookInputJSON` tool events, subagent fields | `user_prompt`, `agent_response`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `file_read`, `usage` |

**The load-bearing difference is not the discriminator — it is the shape of the change report.**
One format hands over a *set* of files at the end; the other hands over a *stream* of individual
edits. That is why the seam is a **normalizer**, not a shared schema: a schema would have had to
pick one of those two shapes and lose information from the other. `goose`'s undocumented `type: 5`
is retained here deliberately as a real, in-repo example of the "unknown events must not crash"
requirement — we do not know what it means, and the integration must not care.

### 16.4 Revised architecture

```
                       ┌─ readers/entire-protocol.ts   ORIGINAL (integer-tagged)
detectFormat(lines) ──►├─ readers/acme-events.ts       NEW (string-tagged)
   sniff, never guess  └─ registry: a third format is one file and one row
                                    │
                                    ▼   one shape, one normalizer, one adjudicator
  AgentSession {
    format, session_id, agent, repo,
    claimed_changes[],    // path, kind, summary, source line number
    lifecycle { started, ended },
    checkpoints[],        // checkpoint_id, git_commit, intent, open_questions[]
    unknown_events[],     // { name, count, first_line } -- recorded, never thrown
    complete: boolean,    // ended cleanly AND no unparseable tail
    degraded[]            // every per-line failure, verbatim
  }
```

Format detection sniffs the first parseable record and **refuses rather than guesses** when the
discriminator is absent or contradictory — the same rule §7 already applies to an ambiguous
symbol. A refusal lands in `degraded[]`; it never produces an empty-but-confident session.

`verify_change` now gathers two sources instead of one:

- `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` → `changed_files`, **`deterministic`** (unchanged)
- the session transcript → `claimed_changes`, **`claimed`** (a new `Confidence` value)

### 16.5 Why the new result is safe — the additive-only invariant

This is the design's spine and the answer to *"why is the new result safe."*

> **Session evidence is additive-only.** It may only ever *add* findings. It never discharges a
> `must_update` obligation, never shrinks `out_of_bounds`, and never removes anything.
>
> Therefore, for every contract, every diff and every transcript:
>
> **`severity(verdict │ git + session) ≥ severity(verdict │ git)`**
>
> — and it holds **by construction, not by test coverage.**

The failure mode this forecloses is specific and was identified before implementation. A
truncated transcript parses *fewer* `file_changed` events. Fewer events means fewer detected
edits. If claimed edits were allowed to satisfy obligations, fewer of them would mean fewer
`forgotten` findings — and **an incomplete input would silently convert a FAIL into a PASS.**
That is the single most dangerous thing this change could have introduced, and the additive-only
rule makes it unrepresentable: a claim has no power to remove a finding, so no amount of missing
transcript can lower a verdict below its git-only baseline.

A property test asserts the inequality across every fixture, rather than asserting it at a
handful of chosen points.

### 16.6 New finding classes, and their honest weight

| Finding | Meaning | Weight | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `out_of_bounds_by_claim` | the agent **itself reports** editing a file the contract forbids | **FAIL** | An admission against interest, checked against a *deterministic* `allowed_files` set. The breach is established by the contract, not by the transcript's reliability — so it stands regardless of what git shows. |
| `unverified_claims` | a claimed edit git cannot confirm | **WARN** | Uncertain evidence. §12's standing rule — *uncertain evidence never alone drives a FAIL* — already governs `TESTS` and `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`; a self-report is no stronger. |
| `unclaimed_changes` | git shows an edit the transcript never mentions | **WARN** | An out-of-band edit, but a transcript is legitimately allowed to be partial, so this cannot be a failure on its own. |

And a new `evidence_basis` field on the verdict, so the *interface itself* distinguishes complete
from incomplete context:

| `evidence_basis` | When | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `deterministic` | no session supplied — today's behaviour | none |
| `reconciled` | both git and session present and cross-checked | none |
| `claimed_only` | no git evidence for the change set (base absent, or a session from another machine) | **PASS is unreachable** — floored at WARN, with `degraded[]` naming the reason |

`claimed_only` is how the design obeys *"never present incomplete context as a complete or
authoritative result"*: the restriction is enforced in the verdict type, not left to the caller
to remember.

### 16.7 What is preserved, concretely

- **`verify_change({ contract_id })` with no session is byte-identical to today.** New buckets
  default to empty arrays; `evidence_basis` is `deterministic`.
- **All 33 existing tests keep passing unmodified.** This is the direct reason every new field is
  additive and optional — the `adjudicate` impact run named three test files among its five direct
  callers *before* the first edit.
- **Existing Checkpoint behaviour is unchanged, and gains a second source.** Transcript
  `checkpoint_created.open_questions[]` are normalised into the **same `KnownTrap` type** already
  produced by `entire checkpoint explain`. Nothing about the CLI-sourced path changes. The fixture
  makes this concrete: `"Should expiry or disabled state take precedence in user-facing errors?"`
  is exactly an unresolved risk, in exactly the shape §7 step 3 already consumes. This also closes
  §14.4's open risk, that the `known_traps` happy path had never been exercised end to end.
- **One implementation, not one per format.** Detection and two thin readers are the only
  format-aware code. Normalisation, reconciliation, adjudication, formatting and both transports
  are shared. Adding a third format is one reader file and one registry row.

### 16.8 Test matrix

The card mandates the first four; the last two are ours.

| Layer | Fixture | Asserts |
|---|---|---|
| Original format | `session-entire-protocol.jsonl` (built from the real `EventJSON` / `AgentSessionJSON` shapes, integer types) | changed files extracted from the batch summary *and* from `tool_input.file_path`; lifecycle resolved |
| New format | `track-3-agent-session.jsonl` (attached, unmodified) | three `file_changed` events collapse to two distinct paths; checkpoint and `open_questions[]` captured; session marked complete |
| Unknown events | `session-unknown-events.jsonl` — `event: "thinking_block"`, `event: "mcp_tool_call"`, and original-format `type: 99` | no throw; counted in `unknown_events[]`; the session remains usable |
| Incomplete input | `session-incomplete.jsonl` — final line truncated mid-JSON, no `session_ended` | `complete: false`; partial claims still returned; `degraded[]` populated; **the session is not discarded** |
| Detection refusal | empty file, non-JSONL text, contradictory discriminators | lands in `degraded[]`; no confident empty session |
| **Monotonicity property** | every fixture above, crossed with the existing contract fixtures | **`severity(git + session) ≥ severity(git)`** — the §16.5 invariant |

### 16.9 Files touched, each justified by §16.2

**New** — `src/evidence/session/{detect,normalize,index}.ts`,
`src/evidence/session/readers/{entire-protocol,acme-events}.ts`, their tests, and the four new
fixtures.

**Modified**

| File | Change | Why the graph says this is safe |
|---|---|---|
| `src/types.ts` | `AgentSession`, `ClaimedChange`; `Confidence += "claimed"`; `Provenance.source += "transcript"`; three new `Verdict` buckets; `evidence_basis`; `Policy.fail_on += "out_of_bounds_by_claim"` | 8 type consumers, all reached through `adjudicate`; every addition is optional so none break |
| `src/adjudicate/adjudicate.ts` | additive claim reconciliation; **still a pure function** | 5 direct callers, 3 of them tests — hence additive-only |
| `src/core.ts` | `verify` and `propose` gain an optional `session` | the single consumer of `changedSince` and `knownTraps` |
| `src/cli.ts`, `src/server.ts` | `--session <path>` / a `session` property on both tool schemas | both are direct callers of `verify`; omitting either makes the feature unreachable |
| `src/format.ts` | render the new buckets and an `evidence_basis` banner | presentation only, as with §15.2's drift filter |
| `src/evidence/exec.ts` | **add** `parseJsonl()` | a new export; `parseJson`'s 2 callers are untouched |

`src/evidence/git.ts` is **not** modified. That is a graph finding, not an oversight.

### 16.10 Approaches rejected

| Approach | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| Transcript *replaces* git when supplied | Destroys the deterministic guarantee. A self-reported or truncated transcript would then drive verdicts directly — the exact hazard §16.5 exists to foreclose. |
| A separate `verify_session` tool | The card explicitly forbids duplicating the implementation per format, and it forfeits reconciliation, which is where the value is: neither source alone can produce `out_of_bounds_by_claim` or `unclaimed_changes`. |
| Treat `git diff` as "format 1" and the transcript as "format 2" | Reads as dodging the constraint. The card says *"a new transcript and lifecycle event format"* — two transcript formats. |

### 16.11 Open risks going into implementation

- **Claim-to-path normalisation across repository roots.** A transcript records paths relative to
  *its* repo (`src/checkout/apply_coupon.ts` in the fixture, from `example/checkout-service`).
  Reconciling those against this repo's paths is only sound when the roots match; when they do not,
  the honest answer is `claimed_only` plus a `degraded[]` entry, not a fabricated mapping.
- **`unclaimed_changes` will be noisy on a real session**, because a human editing alongside an
  agent produces exactly that signal. It is WARN-only for this reason, but the ranking may need
  §15.2's treatment.
- The `entire-protocol` reader's integer lifecycle mapping is derived from three observed values.
  Any other integer is deliberately unknown, not assumed.
ENDOFSECTION

## Noon Curveball: what changed and how we adapted

**Track 3 card — "The agent changed its format."** Full technical detail, with the graph output
that shaped it, is [`DESIGN.md` §16](DESIGN.md). Written in a fresh session reconstructed from
Checkpoint `0b7f487b6e75`, with graph impact run **before** the first edit.

### The assumption the Curveball invalidated

> **entire-guard assumed the record of what an agent changed is a single source with no format at
> all** — `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` against a local working tree.

Two assumptions inside that, both now false:

- **Singular.** The agent's own transcript is also a record, and a *different* one.
- **Format-free.** The record needs parsing, so its format can change underneath us — and has.

A third consequence the first two hide: **a transcript can describe work `git` on this machine
cannot see at all.** A verification path that only reads a local diff cannot represent that
situation, let alone judge it safely.

So the Curveball is not a request for a parser. It asks us to stop treating *"what changed"* as a
fact and start treating it as **evidence with a provenance and a confidence** — the discipline we
already applied to graph relations and checkpoint traps, and had never applied to the diff.

### How the design changed

A session-transcript evidence provider, added *beside* the git adapter rather than inside it:
format detection → two thin readers → **one** normaliser → **one** adjudicator.

| | Original — Entire external-agent protocol | New — AcmeCode 1.4.2 (attached fixture) |
|---|---|---|
| Discriminator | `type`, an **integer** (`1` spawn, `2` prompt, `3` stop; goose emits an undocumented `5`) | `event`, a **string** (10 kinds) |
| Changed files | `modified_files[] / new_files[] / deleted_files[]` — a **batch summary** | `file_changed` — a **stream**, one event per edit |
| Checkpoint | minted by Entire from the session | `checkpoint_created` with `intent`, `summary`, `open_questions[]` |

The load-bearing difference is not the discriminator but the *shape of the change report* — a set
versus a stream. That is why the seam is a normaliser and not a shared schema: a schema would have
had to pick one shape and discard information from the other. **Only detection and the two readers
are format-aware**; normalisation, reconciliation, adjudication, formatting and both transports are
shared. A third format is one reader file and one registry row.

Reconciling two sources produces three findings **neither source can produce alone**:

| Finding | Weight |
|---|---|
| `out_of_bounds_by_claim` — the agent itself reports editing a file the contract forbids | **FAIL** (an admission against interest, checked against a deterministic radius) |
| `unverified_claims` — a claimed edit git cannot confirm | WARN (uncertain evidence never alone drives a FAIL) |
| `unclaimed_changes` — git shows an edit the transcript never mentions | WARN (a transcript may legitimately be partial) |

### Why the new result is safe

> **Session evidence is additive-only.** It may only *add* findings — never discharge a
> `must_update` obligation, never shrink `out_of_bounds`, never remove anything. Therefore
> **`severity(git + session) >= severity(git)`**, by construction rather than by test coverage.

The hazard this forecloses is exact. A truncated transcript parses **fewer** `file_changed`
events; fewer events means fewer detected edits. Had claims been allowed to satisfy obligations,
fewer of them would mean fewer `forgotten` findings, and **an incomplete input would silently turn
a FAIL into a PASS** — the precise failure class this product exists to catch, introduced by the
fix for it. Additive-only makes that unrepresentable. A property test asserts the inequality across
every fixture rather than at a few chosen points.

Second safety rule, enforced in the type rather than left to the caller: a verdict carries
`evidence_basis` of `deterministic`, `reconciled` or `claimed_only`, and **`claimed_only` can never
be PASS** — floored at WARN with `degraded[]` naming the reason. Incomplete context is never
presented as authoritative.

### Existing behaviour preserved

- `verify_change({ contract_id })` with no session is **byte-identical to today**; new buckets
  default empty, `evidence_basis` is `deterministic`.
- **All 33 pre-Curveball tests pass unmodified.** That is *why* every new field is additive and
  optional: the pre-edit impact run on `adjudicate` named 5 direct callers, **3 of them test files**.
- **Checkpoint behaviour is unchanged and gains a second source.** Transcript
  `checkpoint_created.open_questions[]` normalise into the **same `KnownTrap` type** the
  `entire checkpoint explain` path already produces. This also closes a pre-Curveball open risk —
  that the `known_traps` happy path had never been exercised end to end.

### What the graph told us *not* to change

Impact ran on `changedSince`, `parseJson`, `knownTraps`, `verify` and `adjudicate` before any edit;
raw JSON is committed under `evidence/curveball/`. It narrowed the change twice:

- `changedSince` has exactly one caller (`core.ts:100 verify`), so **`src/evidence/git.ts` is not
  modified at all** — the new source goes beside it, not inside it.
- `parseJson` has two callers, so it gains a **sibling** `parseJsonl()` rather than a modification.

The blast radius is entirely within `mcp/entire-guard/src`. **No Go module is touched.**

### Tests

The card's four mandated categories, plus two of ours: **original format** · **new format** ·
**unknown events** (`event: "thinking_block"`, and an integer `type: 99`) · **incomplete input**
(final line truncated mid-JSON, no `session_ended`) · detection refusal on ambiguous input ·
**the monotonicity property test** behind the safety claim above.

Track 3's card requires impact analysis **before** the change, and states that graph use which
happens after implementation scores in the partial band. These six artifacts were captured in a
fresh agent session, reconstructed from Checkpoint `0b7f487b6e75`, with **no source file edited

the plan, so the reasoning can be checked rather than taken on trust.

## 0. Search — locate the code the Curveball lands on — `00-search.json`

```bash
entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format json \
  --query "determine which files the agent actually changed and adjudicate them against the contract"
```

Rank 1 is `mcp/entire-guard/src/adjudicate/adjudicate.ts:39` — `adjudicate`, matched on
`path`, `body`, `symbol-name`, `signature`, `graph:callers` and `complete-symbol`. Located from a
plain-language description of the Curveball, without naming a file.

```bash
entire graph impact --symbol changedSince --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol parseJson    --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol knownTraps   --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol verify       --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
entire graph impact --symbol adjudicate   --repo . --depth 2 --profile full --format json --max-context-bytes 65536
```

`--max-context-bytes` is raised to 65536 because the 4096 default truncates the radius **with no
error** — the exact silent-clipping failure this product exists to catch.

| # | Symbol | Focus | Callers | What it changed about the plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `changedSince` | `src/evidence/git.ts:30` | 1 direct (`core.ts:100 verify`), 2 transitive (`cli.ts:31 main`, `server.ts`) | **`src/evidence/git.ts` is not modified at all.** The new evidence source is added *beside* it in `verify`, not inside it. This narrowed the change. |
| 2 | `parseJson` | `src/evidence/exec.ts:54` | 2 direct (`knownTraps`, `impact`) | Give it a **sibling** `parseJsonl()` rather than modify it, so neither existing caller is disturbed. |
| 3 | `knownTraps` | `src/evidence/checkpoints.ts:106` | 1 direct (`core.ts:26 propose`) | The trap path has a single entry point, so adding a second trap *source* stays local. |
| 4 | `verify` | `src/core.ts:100` | 2 direct (`cli.ts:31 main`, `server.ts`) | **Both** transports must gain the new optional input, or the feature is unreachable from one of them. |
| 5 | `adjudicate` | `src/adjudicate/adjudicate.ts:39` | 5 direct — **3 of them test files** (`adjudicate.test.ts`, `build.test.ts`, `e2e.test.ts`) | The decisive finding: every new field must be **additive and optional**, so all 33 pre-Curveball tests keep compiling and passing unmodified. |

Both are *negative* results — things the graph told us **not** to touch, which is the harder half
of impact analysis to get from reading code:

1. **`git.ts` needs no change.** `changedSince` has exactly one caller. Nothing about how the

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

## The two tools

### `propose_change({ symbol, depth?, repo?, allow_dirty? })`

Refuses on a dirty tree (a contract against an already-modified tree adjudicates nothing),
pins `base_sha`, then runs graph impact and checkpoint recall to produce:

| Field | Meaning | Confidence | Verdict weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| `must_update` | depth-1 callers in *other* files | deterministic (`CALLS`) | **FAIL** if untouched |
| `allowed_files` | the proven blast radius | deterministic | **FAIL** if you edit outside it |
| `drift_candidates` | co-change history (`FILE_CHANGES_WITH`) | **heuristic** | WARN only |
| `known_traps` | unresolved work recalled from checkpoints | **heuristic** | WARN only |
| `degraded` | what could **not** be determined, and why | — | disclosed, never hidden |

The contract is written to `.entire-guard/contracts/<id>.json` — on disk deliberately, so it
survives a server restart, survives a fresh agent session, and can be opened by a human.

### `verify_change({ contract_id?, repo? })`

Loads the contract, diffs the working tree against `base_sha`, runs `entire graph diff` for
entity-level semantic changes, and adjudicates:

- `out_of_bounds` = edited − allowed → **FAIL**
- `forgotten` = obliged − edited → **FAIL** ← the finding a diff cannot show
- `drift_candidates` untouched → **WARN** (heuristic)
- `known_traps` in edited files → **WARN** (heuristic)

**Every finding prints the literal command that produced it.** Copy any line out of the output
and re-run it yourself.

## Design rules this code actually enforces

1. **Degrade loudly, never fabricate.** If the radius could not be measured, no contract is
   written — we do not invent one. Everything uncertain lands in `degraded[]`.
2. **A heuristic relation never causes a FAIL.** `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` and `TESTS` are labelled
   heuristic by the graph itself; they warn, and the output says so.
3. **The adjudicator is a pure function.** No I/O, no clock, no network, no model. Same inputs
   produce the same verdict byte for byte, and it is unit-testable with zero CLI dependency.
4. **Policy is one object** (`DEFAULT_POLICY` in `src/types.ts`), not thresholds scattered
   through the code — so a new constraint is a config change, not a rewrite.
5. **stdout is sacred.** MCP stdio speaks JSON-RPC over stdout; every diagnostic goes to stderr.
6. **`--max-context-bytes` is raised to 65536 and truncation is detected.** The 4096 default
   silently clips the blast radius with no error, which would corrupt the exact claim this
   product rests on.

## Setup

```bash
cd mcp/entire-guard
npm install
npm run build
npm test          # 14 tests
```

Register with any MCP client. A project-level `.mcp.json` already exists at the repo root:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "entire-guard": { "command": "node", "args": ["./mcp/entire-guard/dist/server.js"] } } }
```

## CLI (CI and fallback)

The same core runs without a protocol in the way — a PR check needs a verdict and an exit code,
not an MCP session:

```bash
node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js propose "agents/entire-agent-kiro/internal/protocol/protocol.go:63"
node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify --json
# exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 WARN, 2 FAIL, 3 error
```

## Known limitations

- `TESTS` and `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` are heuristic relations. Labelled as such; never sole cause of a FAIL.
- Trap extraction is keyword-based, so recall is limited — an open risk phrased unusually is missed.
  Chosen deliberately over an LLM for determinism and offline operation.
- Blast radius is bounded at depth 2; a genuinely transitive break at depth 3+ is out of scope.
- Dynamic dispatch, reflection and codegen are invisible to a static graph.
- Adjudication is path-level, not hunk-level: editing a file anywhere satisfies its obligation.
- Single-repo only. Cross-repo impact is a next step, not a claim.

## Live verification, after implementation

The impact analysis above ran before any edit. This section records what the implementation it
produced actually does, so the two can be compared.

```bash
cd mcp/entire-guard && npm install && npm run build && npm test
# -> 82 passing, 0 failing   (33 pre-Curveball tests unchanged, 49 new)
```

Every fixture through the real CLI, from the repository root:

```bash
node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js propose adjudicate --repo . --allow-dirty \
  --session mcp/entire-guard/test/fixtures/track-3-agent-session.jsonl

for f in track-3-agent-session session-entire-protocol \
         session-original-unknown-events session-unknown-events session-incomplete; do
  node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify --repo . \
    --session mcp/entire-guard/test/fixtures/$f.jsonl --json
done
```

| Fixture | Format detected | `evidence_basis` | Disclosed in `degraded[]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track-3-agent-session.jsonl` (attached) | `acme-events` | `reconciled` | repository mismatch against this checkout |
| `session-entire-protocol.jsonl` | `entire-protocol` | `reconciled` | repository mismatch |
| `session-original-unknown-events.jsonl` | `entire-protocol` | `reconciled` | `type:5 x1 (line 2)`, `type:99 x1 (line 3)`, `hook:pre-compact x1 (line 4)` |
| `session-unknown-events.jsonl` | `acme-events` | `reconciled` | `thinking_block`, `mcp_tool_call`, `subagent_spawned` |
| `session-incomplete.jsonl` | `acme-events` | `reconciled` | `line 5 could not be parsed (Unterminated string in JSON...)`; no session-end event |

Five transcripts, two formats, one adjudicator. Unknown events named rather than swallowed; the
truncated line named rather than silently shortening the session.

### The safety invariant, executed rather than asserted

Two runs against a contract whose `base_sha` is deliberately not a commit in this repository:

```
$ node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify ct-claimonly-demo --repo .
cannot diff against deadbeef...: fatal: bad object deadbeef...
$ echo $?
3
```

Unchanged behaviour: with no second source there is nothing to fall back on, so the original
failure stands. Now with the transcript:

```
VERDICT: WARN - contract honoured, but with unverified risk
EVIDENCE BASIS: claimed_only - no git evidence for this change set, so nothing could be
                confirmed against disk. This CANNOT BE A PASS.

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS (2) - claimed in the transcript, absent from the diff. [CLAIMED]
  - src/checkout/apply_coupon.ts
    claimed modified at transcript line 7, but the diff against deadbeef... does not show it
```

That is the case the Curveball is really about — a transcript describing work this machine cannot
see in git — and the verdict is **WARN, never PASS**, with the reason stated in the output.

Monotonicity on the real repository, which is the claim that matters:

```
$ node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify --repo .                     ; echo $?   # 2  (FAIL)
$ node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify --repo . --session <any>     ; echo $?   # 2  (FAIL)
```

Never lower. The 84-case property test in `src/adjudicate/claims.test.ts` asserts the same
inequality across a matrix of contracts, diffs and transcripts.

### MCP surface

```bash
printf '%s\n%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"smoke","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  | node mcp/entire-guard/dist/server.js
```

`initialize` returns `entire-guard 0.1.0`; `tools/list` returns both tools, each now exposing
`session`. No stdout pollution — the JSON-RPC stream stays clean.

### One graph claim worth reporting honestly

The `adjudicate` impact run listed `evidence/README.md` as a depth-1 caller, because the graph
matched the symbol name in prose. That row is real in the contract too: it appears as a
`must_update` obligation and therefore in `forgotten`. It is pre-existing, unrelated to
transcripts, and left disclosed rather than filtered — filtering non-source obligations changes
what a FAIL means, which is a design decision and not a patch to slip into a Curveball response.

## 17. Curveball build log — what implementation changed about §16

*Appended after implementing §16. Everything above §17 was written before code existed;
everything here was learned by running it. `npm test` -> **82 passing, 0 failing** (33
pre-Curveball unchanged, 49 new).*

### 17.1 §16 survived implementation intact

Unusually, the architecture in §16.4 needed no revision. The reason is the §16.2 impact analysis:
the two negative findings (`git.ts` untouched, `parseJson` gains a sibling) removed the two places
where the change could have sprawled, before a line was written.

| §16 claim | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `src/evidence/git.ts` not modified | Held. Untouched. |
| `parseJson` gains a sibling, not a change | Held. `parseJsonl` added; both existing callers untouched. |
| All 33 existing tests pass unmodified | Held. Not one existing test file was edited. |
| One normaliser, two thin readers | Held. Format-aware code is confined to `detect.ts` and the two readers. |
| Additive-only safety invariant | Held, and now executable: 84-case property test. |

### 17.2 Five things the build added that §16 did not specify

1. **A second unknown-events fixture.** §16.8 planned one fixture mixing a string `event` with an
   integer `type: 99`. That is impossible: such a file is *ambiguous* by the detection rule and is
   correctly refused. Split into `session-unknown-events.jsonl` (new format) and
   `session-original-unknown-events.jsonl` (original). Stronger than planned — unknown events are
   now covered in **both** formats rather than one.

2. **`EventJSON` cannot contribute a claimed change.** It carries `tool_input` but **no
   `tool_name`**, so a `file_path` on one of those records cannot be shown to be an edit rather
   than a read. Only `HookInputJSON`, which does carry `tool_name`, can. §16.3 had assumed tool
   events were a usable claim source in the original format; they are only usable in one of its
   three record shapes. Discovered by reading `types.go`, not by guessing.

3. **`git_unavailable` had to be plumbed, not inferred.** §16.5 named `claimed_only` but not how
   it arises. It arises when `changedSince` throws — a `base_sha` absent from this checkout. The
   rule that fell out: **without a transcript the original failure still propagates** (preserving
   existing behaviour exactly), and only *with* one does it degrade to `claimed_only`.

4. **A repository-mismatch caveat.** §16.11 flagged cross-root path normalisation as an open risk.
   Implemented as detection plus disclosure rather than remapping: when the transcript's `repo`
   does not match the contract's `repo_root`, the caveat is emitted next to the claim findings it
   explains. Paths are never rewritten — a guessed mapping would be a fabrication.

5. **`basisNote()` in the formatter.** A bare `claimed_only` label does not satisfy "the interface
   must clearly distinguish complete from incomplete context" for a reader who has never seen the
   type, so the constraint is spelled out in words where the verdict is read:
   *"This CANNOT BE A PASS."*

### 17.3 One process deviation, disclosed

`loadSession` was written before its test. On noticing, it was **deleted** and re-driven from
`load.test.ts` — the failing test observed first (`has no exported member 'loadSession'`), then
reimplemented. Recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because "the code compiled, the tests
passed, the feature did nothing" (§15.1) happened in this project precisely where a shape was
assumed instead of observed.

### 17.4 Wording defect found by running it

The repository-mismatch caveat originally ended *"so out-of-bounds claims below may reflect that
mismatch"* — but in the `claimed_only` demonstration there were no out-of-bounds claims, only
unverified ones. The message asserted the existence of findings that were not present. Corrected
to "the claim findings below". Small, but it is the same class as §15.1: output that reads
plausibly while describing something that is not there.

### 17.5 Open risks after implementation

- `unclaimed_changes` reported 24 rows against the live dirty tree. Honest, and WARN-only, but on
  a real session it will need §15.2's ranking treatment.
- Edit-tool detection in the original format is a name-shape heuristic. It errs narrow by design:
  a missed writer loses a claim, which under additive-only can never make a verdict more
  permissive.
- `evidence/README.md` appears as a `must_update` obligation because the graph matched
  `adjudicate` in prose. Pre-existing and unrelated to transcripts; left disclosed rather than
  filtered, because filtering non-source obligations changes what a FAIL means.
- The automated suite still does not shell out to `entire` or `git`. That seam was exercised by
  hand and the commands and observed results are recorded in `evidence/curveball/README.md`.

Implementation is complete and verified. **Nothing committed** — the working tree is staged for your review.

## What was built

One new subsystem, `src/evidence/session/`, plus additive changes to seven existing files:

| | |

`detect.ts` | Sniffs the format. **Refuses rather than guesses** — an absent or contradictory discriminator lands in `degraded[]` |


| Fixture | Detected | Basis | Disclosed |
|---|---|---|---|
`track-3-agent-session.jsonl` (attached) | `acme-events` | reconciled | repo mismatch |
`session-entire-protocol.jsonl` | `entire-protocol` | reconciled | repo mismatch |
`session-original-unknown-events.jsonl` | `entire-protocol` | reconciled | `type:5`, `type:99`, `hook:pre-compact` |
`session-unknown-events.jsonl` | `acme-events` | reconciled | `thinking_block`, `mcp_tool_call`, `subagent_spawned` |
`session-incomplete.jsonl` | `acme-events` | reconciled | `line 5 ... Unterminated string`; no session-end |

**The safety claim, executed rather than asserted.** On a contract whose `base_sha` isn't a commit here: without a transcript, `verify` fails with git's own error, exit 3 — unchanged. With one, it degrades to `EVIDENCE BASIS: claimed_only ... This CANNOT BE A PASS.` and returns WARN. Monotonicity on the live repo: exit 2 without a session, exit 2 with each session. Never lower. An 84-case property test asserts the same inequality.

1. **`loadSession` was written before its test.** I deleted it, watched `load.test.ts` fail, and reimplemented. Recorded in DESIGN.md §17.3 rather than quietly fixed.

with no format at all: `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` against a local
working tree. Two things were baked into that and both are now false.

  Singular    - the agent's own transcript is also a record, and a different one.
  Format-free - the record needs parsing, so its format can change under us.

And a third consequence those two hide: a transcript can describe work that
git on this machine cannot see at all. A verification path that only reads a
local diff cannot represent that situation, let alone judge it safely.

So Track 3 is not a request for a parser. It asks us to stop treating "what
changed" as a fact and start treating it as evidence with a provenance and a
confidence - the discipline already applied to graph relations and checkpoint
traps, and never applied to the diff.

GRAPH IMPACT, RUN BEFORE EDITING

Six artifacts committed under evidence/curveball/, captured at clean 28a5705
before a source file was touched. It narrowed the change twice, and both are
negative results - things the graph said NOT to touch:

  changedSince -> 1 direct caller (core.ts:100 verify). So src/evidence/git.ts
                  is not modified at all; the new source goes beside it.
  parseJson    -> 2 direct callers. So it gains a sibling parseJsonl(), not a
                  modification.
  adjudicate   -> 5 direct callers, 3 of them test files. The decisive finding:
                  every new field must be additive and optional.

co_changes and siblings are 0 on all five symbols, so no heuristic relation
informed any of it. Blast radius entirely inside mcp/entire-guard/src; no Go
module touched.

HOW THE DESIGN CHANGED

A session-transcript evidence provider added beside the git adapter:
format detection -> two thin readers -> one normaliser -> one adjudicator.

  ORIGINAL  Entire external-agent protocol. Numeric EventJSON.type (1 spawn,
            2 prompt, 3 stop; goose emits an undocumented 5), HookInputJSON
            hook_type + tool_name, AgentSessionJSON modified/new/deleted_files
            as a BATCH SUMMARY.
  NEW       AcmeCode 1.4.2. String-tagged event envelope, file_changed
            STREAMED one event per edit, checkpoint_created with
            open_questions[].

The load-bearing difference is not the discriminator but the shape of the
change report - a set versus a stream. That is why the seam is a normaliser
and not a shared schema: a schema would have had to pick one shape and discard
information from the other. Only detect.ts and the two readers are
format-aware; normalisation, reconciliation, adjudication, formatting and both
transports are shared. A third format is one reader file and one registry row.

Reconciling two sources yields three findings neither can produce alone:

  out_of_bounds_by_claim  the agent itself reports editing a file the contract
                          forbids -> FAIL (an admission against interest,
                          checked against a deterministic radius)
  unverified_claims       claimed, absent from the diff -> WARN
  unclaimed_changes       in the diff, never mentioned -> WARN

WHY THE NEW RESULT IS SAFE

  Session evidence is ADDITIVE-ONLY. It may only add findings - never
  discharge a must_update obligation, never shrink out_of_bounds, never
  remove anything. Therefore severity(git + session) >= severity(git),
  by construction rather than by test coverage.

The hazard this forecloses is exact. A truncated transcript parses fewer
file_changed events, so it yields fewer claims. Had claims been allowed to
satisfy obligations, fewer of them would mean fewer `forgotten` findings, and
an incomplete input would silently turn a FAIL into a PASS - the precise
failure class this product exists to catch, introduced by the fix for it.

Second rule, enforced in the type rather than left to a caller's memory: every
verdict carries evidence_basis of deterministic | reconciled | claimed_only,
and claimed_only can never be PASS - floored at WARN with the reason in
degraded[].

TESTS: 33 -> 82

The card's four categories, and the format-plural ones covered in BOTH formats
rather than only the new one:

  original format   4  claims from the batch summary and from an edit-shaped
                       tool; a readFile is NOT counted as a change
  new format        4  3 file_changed events collapse to 2 distinct paths;
                       checkpoint open_questions captured
  unknown events    4  thinking_block / mcp_tool_call / subagent_spawned, and
                       integer type:5 / type:99 / hook:pre-compact - recorded,
                       never thrown, real edit beside them still lands
  incomplete input  3  session NOT discarded: intact file_changed survives,
                       complete:false, degraded names line 5
  jsonl isolation   4  per-line failure; blanks are not failures
  detection refusal 4  empty, non-JSONL, and both discriminators present ->
                       refused into degraded[], never guessed
  reconciliation   11  the three findings, the FAIL/WARN split, claimed_only
  trap recall       5  transcript open questions -> the same KnownTrap type
  rendering         5  [CLAIMED] labels, evidence-basis banner
  SAFETY PROPERTY   1  84 assertions: 3 contracts x 4 diffs x 7 transcripts

git diff --stat -- '*.test.ts' is empty: not one pre-existing test file was
edited to accommodate this. That is what the pre-edit adjudicate impact run
bought.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT

All five transcripts through the real CLI. propose with the new-format
transcript returned KNOWN TRAPS (1) - "Should expiry or disabled state take
precedence in user-facing errors?" - sourced from checkpoint_created, where
this repo's own checkpoints yielded none for that radius.

The claimed_only floor proved live on a contract whose base_sha is not a
commit here: without a transcript verify fails with git's own error and exit 3
(unchanged); with one it degrades to claimed_only, lists both claims as
UNVERIFIED CLAIMS, and returns WARN, never PASS. Monotonicity on the real
repo: exit 2 without a session, exit 2 with each session. Never lower.

MCP re-verified: initialize -> entire-guard 0.1.0, both tools expose session,
no stdout pollution.

EXISTING BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED

verify_change({contract_id}) with no session is behaviourally unchanged - same
status, same findings, same exit code, new buckets empty, evidence_basis
"deterministic". It is NOT byte-identical: the rendered verdict gains one
EVIDENCE BASIS line. Stated precisely rather than rounded up.

Checkpoint behaviour is unchanged and gains a second source: transcript
open_questions[] normalise into the same KnownTrap type the CLI path produces.
That also closes a pre-Curveball open risk - the known_traps happy path had
never been exercised end to end.

THREE THINGS CORRECTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED

1. loadSession was written before its test. Deleted, the failing test observed,
   then reimplemented. Recorded rather than quietly fixed.
2. The repo-mismatch caveat said "out-of-bounds claims below" when the
   claimed_only run had only unverified ones - output asserting findings that
   were not there. Same class as the known_traps bug this project already
   caught in itself.
3. "byte-identical" was an overclaim; both docs now name the one added line.

ONE PLAN DEVIATION THAT IMPROVED THINGS

The design specified a single unknown-events fixture mixing a string event with
an integer type:99. That file is ambiguous by our own detection rule and is
correctly refused - so it was impossible to write. Split into two fixtures,
which means unknown events are now covered in both formats rather than one.

OPEN RISKS

- Claimed paths are relative to the transcript's own repository. Mismatch is
  detected and disclosed beside the findings it explains; paths are NOT
  remapped, because a guessed mapping would be a fabrication.
- Edit-tool detection in the original format is a name-shape heuristic. Errs
  narrow: a missed writer loses a claim, which under additive-only can never
  make a verdict more permissive.
- EventJSON carries tool_input but no tool_name, so a file_path there cannot be
  shown to be an edit rather than a read. Deliberately not counted.
- unclaimed_changes is noisy on a live session (a human editing alongside an
  agent produces exactly that signal). WARN-only for that reason.
- entire graph impact matched `adjudicate` in the prose of evidence/README.md,
  so a Markdown file appears as a must_update obligation and hence in
  forgotten. Pre-existing, unrelated to transcripts, disclosed rather than
  filtered - filtering non-source obligations changes what a FAIL means.
- The suite still does not shell out to entire or git; that seam was exercised
  by hand and the commands and results are recorded in evidence/curveball/.

# entire-guard — a change contract for coding agents

**BTW Buildathon 2026 · Track 3 — Bring Entire to a New Agent or Workflow**

An MCP server that hands a coding agent a **change contract** derived from Entire Graph impact
analysis plus Entire Checkpoint history, then **holds the agent to that contract** by adjudicating
what it actually edited.

Full write-up: [`BUILDATHON.md`](BUILDATHON.md) · Graph evidence: [`evidence/`](evidence/) and
[`evidence/curveball/`](evidence/curveball/README.md)

---

## The problem

An agent changes a function. It edits files it shouldn't have, and misses one it should have. A
`git diff` shows you the first mistake. It **structurally cannot** show you the second, because the
evidence for a forgotten caller is an *absence*. Both the agent and CI report success. The missing
caller surfaces in production.

## Why this is not a CLI wrapper

> **No Entire command can do what entire-guard does, because no Entire command holds state between
> a proposal and a verification.**

`propose_change` writes a durable contract. `verify_change` adjudicates a later, separate action
against that earlier commitment. The value lives in the *interval between two calls* — a place a
stateless CLI cannot reach. `entire graph impact`, `entire graph diff` and
`entire checkpoint explain` are consumed as evidence inputs, never rebuilt.

Placement is `mcp/entire-guard/` — self-contained, touching neither the `mise` nor the `golangci`
CI. **No Go module is modified by this PR.**

---

## Noon Curveball — "The agent changed its format"

### The assumption it invalidated

> entire-guard assumed the record of what an agent changed is a single source with **no format at
> all**: `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` against a local working tree.

Two things were baked into that, both now false — **singular** (the agent's own transcript is also
a record, and a different one) and **format-free** (the record needs parsing, so its format can
change under us). Plus a third the first two hide: **a transcript can describe work git on this
machine cannot see at all.**

### How the design changed

A session-transcript provider added *beside* the git adapter: format detection → two thin readers →
**one** normaliser → **one** adjudicator.

| | Original — Entire external-agent protocol | New — event envelope (attached fixture) |
|---|---|---|
| Discriminator | `type`, an **integer** | `event`, a **string** |
| Changed files | `modified_files`/`new_files`/`deleted_files` — a **batch summary** | `file_changed` — a **stream**, one per edit |
| Checkpoint | minted by Entire | `checkpoint_created` with `open_questions[]` |

The load-bearing difference is not the discriminator but the *shape of the change report* — a set
versus a stream. That is why the seam is a normaliser, not a shared schema: a schema would have had
to pick one shape and discard information from the other. Only `detect.ts` and the two readers are
format-aware. **A third format is one reader file and one registry row.**

### Why the new result is safe

> **Session evidence is additive-only.** It may only *add* findings — never discharge a
> `must_update` obligation, never shrink `out_of_bounds`, never remove anything. Therefore
> **`severity(git + session) >= severity(git)`**, by construction rather than by test coverage.

The hazard this forecloses is exact. A truncated transcript parses **fewer** `file_changed` events,
so it yields fewer claims. Had claims been allowed to satisfy obligations, fewer of them would mean
fewer `forgotten` findings — and **an incomplete input would silently turn a FAIL into a PASS**, the
very failure class this tool exists to catch, introduced by the fix for it.

Second rule, enforced in the type rather than in a caller's memory: every verdict carries
`evidence_basis` of `deterministic` | `reconciled` | `claimed_only`, and **`claimed_only` can never
be PASS**.

Three findings neither source can produce alone: `out_of_bounds_by_claim` (**FAIL** — an admission
against interest, checked against a deterministic radius), `unverified_claims` (WARN),
`unclaimed_changes` (WARN).

### Graph impact, run before editing

Six artifacts in [`evidence/curveball/`](evidence/curveball/README.md), captured at clean `28a5705`
**before a source file was touched**. It narrowed the change twice, and both are *negative* results:

- `changedSince` → 1 direct caller, so **`src/evidence/git.ts` is not modified at all**
- `parseJson` → 2 callers, so it gains a **sibling** `parseJsonl()`, not a modification
- `adjudicate` → 5 direct callers, **3 of them test files** — hence every new field is additive and
  optional

`co_changes` and `siblings` are **0** on all five symbols, so no heuristic relation informed any of
it.

### Tests: 33 → 82

The card's four categories, with the format-plural ones covered in **both** formats: original
format · new format · unknown events (`thinking_block`, and integer `type: 99`) · incomplete input
(final line cut mid-JSON) · detection refusal on ambiguous input · **an 84-assertion property test**
for the safety invariant above.

`git diff --stat -- '*.test.ts'` is **empty** — not one pre-existing test file was edited to
accommodate this.

`verify_change({ contract_id })` with no session is **behaviourally unchanged**: same status, same
findings, same exit code. It is *not* byte-identical — the rendered verdict gains one
`EVIDENCE BASIS` line.

---

## Checkpoints

Linked by **ID**, because Entire titles a checkpoint from whichever prompt was active when the
commit landed, so the titles are noise. AI summaries are generated for the last two, so `explain`
opens on Intent / Outcome / Learnings.

| # | Checkpoint | Commit | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `362b7ddbefdc` | `6ac492c` | Initial understanding, intended architecture, and the options rejected |
| 2 | `2463e7d51ae5` | `85c1b9b` | The runnable slice at the pre-noon freeze, plus six assumptions the build invalidated |
| 3 | `0b7f487b6e75` | `28a5705` | **The stable state entering the Curveball** — reconstructed from in a fresh session |
| 4 | `5ce69064166d` | `b517beb` | **The Curveball response**, in a *separate* session (`cbb577fd…` vs `9afea542…`) |

```bash
entire checkpoint explain 0b7f487b6e75 --full     # intent and open risks going in
entire checkpoint explain 5ce69064166d --full     # what changed after the Curveball, and why it is safe
```

---

## Run it

```bash
cd mcp/entire-guard && npm install && npm run build && npm test   # 82 passing

# from the repo root
node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js propose adjudicate --repo . \
  --session mcp/entire-guard/test/fixtures/track-3-agent-session.jsonl
node mcp/entire-guard/dist/cli.js verify --repo . \
  --session mcp/entire-guard/test/fixtures/session-entire-protocol.jsonl
```

Exit codes `0` PASS / `1` WARN / `2` FAIL / `3` error, so it drops straight into a CI check.
`dist/` is not committed, so **build before starting the MCP server**.

## Known limitations, stated rather than hidden

- `TESTS` and `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` are heuristic relations; labelled as such, never the sole cause of
  a FAIL.
- Adjudication is path-level, not hunk-level.
- Claimed paths are relative to the transcript's own repository; a mismatch is detected and
  disclosed beside the findings it explains, but paths are **not** remapped — a guessed mapping
  would be a fabrication.
- Edit-tool detection in the original format is a name-shape heuristic, erring narrow: a missed
  claim can never make a verdict more permissive under additive-only.
- `entire graph impact` matched `adjudicate` in the prose of `evidence/README.md`, so a Markdown
  file appears as a `must_update` obligation. Pre-existing and disclosed rather than filtered —
  filtering non-source obligations changes what a FAIL means.
- The suite does not shell out to `entire` or `git`; that seam was exercised by hand and the
  commands and observed results are recorded in `evidence/curveball/README.md`.

### Design rules the code enforces

1. **Degrade loudly, never fabricate.** If the radius cannot be measured, no contract is written.
2. **A heuristic relation never causes a FAIL.** `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` and `TESTS` are heuristic per
   the graph's own capabilities output; they warn, and the output says so.
3. **The adjudicator is a pure function** — no I/O, no clock, no model. Same inputs, same verdict.
4. **Policy is one object**, so a new constraint is a config change, not a rewrite.
5. **stdout is sacred** — MCP speaks JSON-RPC over it; diagnostics go to stderr.

## Entire Graph findings and verification

Full detail and reproduction commands: [`evidence/README.md`](evidence/README.md).

1. **Search** (`evidence/01-search.json`) — located the adjudication logic from a plain-language
   description.
2. **Impact before a high-risk change** (`evidence/02-impact.json`) — run against our **own**
   `adjudicate`, the highest-risk symbol in the project since every verdict flows through it.
   Found 6 callers: 4 at depth 1, 2 transitively at depth 2.
3. **Final semantic diff of the submitted implementation**
   (`evidence/curveball/06-semantic-diff.json`) — `entire graph diff --base 28a5705 --head HEAD`,
   re-run **after** the Curveball so it describes what is actually being submitted.
   `evidence/03-semantic-diff.json` is the earlier, pre-Curveball run and is kept for comparison
   rather than replaced.

   **28 files with entity-level changes**, and their shape is the argument: `src/types.ts` is the
   largest at 51 — all additive — while the **two format readers together are 5**. Format-aware
   code is the smallest part of the change, which is the "do not duplicate the implementation per
   format" rule measured rather than asserted. `src/evidence/git.ts` does not appear at all,
   independently confirming the prediction the pre-edit `changedSince` impact run made.

   `verify_change` runs this same command on every verdict, so the required artifact *is* a
   product feature.

**Verified against source.** The graph claimed `verify` in `core.ts` calls `adjudicate` at line
110. `grep -n` confirms `adjudicate(` at line 110. Lines 34 and 39 also contain the word but are
prose in comments — the graph correctly did not report them, which is exactly the difference
between structural analysis and text search.
......
That is the exact failure class this product exists to catch — code compiled, tests passed, output
looked right, feature did nothing.

## Noon Curveball: what changed and how we adapted

**Track 3 card — "The agent changed its format."** Written in a fresh session reconstructed from
Checkpoint `0b7f487b6e75`, with graph impact run **before** the first edit. The graph output that
shaped it — six artifacts, the reproduction commands, and the source checks — is committed under
[`evidence/curveball/`](evidence/curveball/README.md).

> **Status.** The design in this section was written and checkpointed **before** any code changed,
> as the card requires. It is now implemented and measured: `npm test` reports **82 passing, 0
> failing** (33 pre-Curveball tests unchanged, 49 new), and every claim below has been run.

### The assumption the Curveball invalidated

> **entire-guard assumed the record of what an agent changed is a single source with no format at
> all** — `git diff --name-only <base_sha>` against a local working tree.

Two assumptions inside that, both now false:

- **Singular.** The agent's own transcript is also a record, and a *different* one.
- **Format-free.** The record needs parsing, so its format can change underneath us — and has.

A third consequence the first two hide: **a transcript can describe work `git` on this machine
cannot see at all.** A verification path that only reads a local diff cannot represent that
situation, let alone judge it safely.

So the Curveball is not a request for a parser. It asks us to stop treating *"what changed"* as a
fact and start treating it as **evidence with a provenance and a confidence** — the discipline we
already applied to graph relations and checkpoint traps, and had never applied to the diff.

### How the design changed

A session-transcript evidence provider, added *beside* the git adapter rather than inside it:
format detection → two thin readers → **one** normaliser → **one** adjudicator.

| | Original — Entire external-agent protocol | New — AcmeCode 1.4.2 (attached fixture) |
|---|---|---|
| Discriminator | `type`, an **integer** (`1` spawn, `2` prompt, `3` stop; goose emits an undocumented `5`) | `event`, a **string** (10 kinds) |
| Changed files | `modified_files[] / new_files[] / deleted_files[]` — a **batch summary** | `file_changed` — a **stream**, one event per edit |

**both format readers combined** | **5** |
